name: pixelcraft
title: PIXELCRAFT — visual quality, UI/UX and interface efficiency
summary: Audits the rendered application (not its source) in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13, desktop, narrow, tablet and landscape viewports: discovers its screens, captures screenshots, measures spacing, alignment, typography, touch targets, control consistency, safe areas, overflow, layout shift, hover/pressed/focus/disabled states, runs axe-core and user journeys (taps, depth, confirmations, feedback time). Scores Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency (100 each) from evidence, with coverage and confidence reported separately; every finding has screen, viewport, selector, measurements, severity, an annotated screenshot and a fix. verify replays the same routes, viewports and journeys, diffs screenshots, proves fixes and refuses score gains from lost coverage. Works on React, Vite, Next.js, static sites and browser games (HTML overlays). Never modifies the app.

limits: Browser emulation (Chromium): iPhone viewports are CSS sizes with emulated safe areas, not Safari/WebKit; attach real-device screenshots as device_evidence to show physical results.
The on-screen keyboard is not emulated: input zoom (font-size < 16 px) is measured; keyboard overlap is not.
Builds are not run inside the sandbox: build the app first and pass its folder, or start it and pass the localhost URL (inside the sandbox allow its port with GITCRAFT_ALLOW_LOCAL_PORTS).
Canvas-drawn content (games) is not described by the DOM: only the HTML overlay is measured; record what you see as judgements.
Taste is not measured: generic or unfinished-looking screens are recorded as judgements (screenshot evidence) by whoever looked at them.
